EASL-EASD-EASO Guidance on MASH-Targeted Pharmacotherapy
  • Source: Journal of Hepatology, 2026
  • Topic: Use of Resmetirom and Semaglutide for Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatohepatitis (MASH)
  • Author(s): European Association for the Study of the Liver, EASL-EASD-EASO Clinical Practice Guideline Panel
Overview: MASLD and MASH
  • Adults with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) and steatohepatitis (MASH) --> risk of cardiometabolic complications
  • Risk of major adverse liver-related outcomes (MALOs) --> cirrhosis, cancer, liver transplantation
  • Non-invasive tests (NITs) can replace liver biopsy to identify patients at high risk of MALOs
Approved Pharmacotherapy Options
  • Resmetirom: 80 mg or 100 mg per os daily
  • Semaglutide: 2.4 mg subcutaneous injection weekly
Diagnostic Criteria: Identifying Treatment Candidates
Non-Invasive Test Thresholds for Significant/Advanced Fibrosis
  • VCTE (Vibration-Controlled Transient Elastography): 10–20 kPa
  • Requires confirmation by repeated testing or additional NIT
  • MRE (Magnetic Resonance Elastography): 3.1–5.0 kPa
  • ELF (Enhanced Liver Fibrosis): 9.8–11.3
  • Ideally confirmed by an additional NIT
Two-Step Clinical Care Pathway
  • First-line: FIB-4 (Fibrosis-4 index) for initial assessment
  • Use in: type 2 diabetes, obesity with cardiometabolic risk, elevated liver enzymes
  • Second-line (if indeterminate FIB-4): VCTE, ELF, or MRE
  • This approach is prognostic and non-inferior to VCTE alone
Concordant NITs Increase Confidence
  • Two or more concordant specific fibrosis NITs --> ↑ accuracy for diagnosing/excluding clinically relevant fibrosis (F2–F3)
  • Discordant results --> intermediate risk of significant fibrosis or future liver-related events
NIT Thresholds for Treatment Eligibility
NIT Significant Fibrosis Range Advanced/Cirrhosis
VCTE-LSM 10–15 kPa >20 kPa
MRE 3.1–4.4 kPa >5 kPa
ELF 9.8–10.5 >11.3
VCTE Prognosis Study Data
  • 16,603 individuals with MASLD studied
  • MALO incidence rates (per 1,000 person-years):
  • LSM <10 kPa: 0.53
  • LSM 10–20 kPa: 6.59
  • LSM >20 kPa: 33.44
Treatment Candidate Selection
Eligibility Criteria for Pharmacotherapy
  • Adults with non-cirrhotic MASH and fibrosis stages 2–3
  • Based on NITs or biopsy
  • Alongside structured lifestyle intervention and optimized comorbidity management
Treatment Selection Algorithm (Fig. 2)
  • Cardiometabolic dominant phenotype --> prioritize semaglutide
  • Liver dominant phenotype --> prioritize resmetirom
Clinical Scenarios Favoring Semaglutide
  • Obesity or overweight with weight-related comorbidities
  • Type 2 diabetes outside glycemic targets
  • Established cardiovascular disease or high CV risk
  • Chronic kidney disease with obesity and/or T2D
Clinical Scenarios Favoring Resmetirom
  • Normal weight or without obesity
  • Already on GLP-1RA for another indication (or intolerant to GLP-1RA)
  • Prominent atherogenic dyslipidemia
  • Preference for oral administration
  • Presence or high risk of sarcopenia
Drug Comparison: Resmetirom vs Semaglutide
Administration
  • Resmetirom: Oral, once daily (80 mg or 100 mg)
  • Semaglutide: Subcutaneous injection, once weekly (2.4 mg)
Metabolic Effects
Effect Resmetirom Semaglutide
Weight Neutral ~10% reduction (72 weeks)
Glycemic control None Significant HbA1c reduction
LDL cholesterol ↓16% Modest improvement
Triglycerides ↓19% ↓ (modest)
Lp(a) ↓35% Minimal effect
HDL cholesterol No change ↑ (modest)
Key Drug Interactions
Resmetirom
  • CYP2C8 inhibitors: Gemfibrozil (contraindicated), Clopidogrel (requires dose reduction)
  • Statins: Dose caps --> rosuvastatin/simvastatin <20 mg; atorvastatin/pravastatin <40 mg
Semaglutide
  • Minimal hepatic drug interactions
  • May delay gastric emptying --> affects oral drug absorption
Contraindications
Resmetirom
  • Decompensated liver disease
  • Active autoimmune hepatitis/primary biliary cholangitis (PBC)
  • Uncontrolled thyroid disease
  • Significant alcohol use
  • Gemfibrozil or cyclosporine use
Semaglutide
  • Personal/family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC)
  • Multiple endocrine neoplasia type 2 (MEN2)
  • Potential for temporary worsening of diabetic retinopathy
Thyroid Considerations
  • Resmetirom: Lowers free T4 by ~14–18% --> baseline TSH required; avoid if uncontrolled thyroid disease
  • Semaglutide: No thyroid concerns (but boxed warning for thyroid C-cell tumors based on rodent data)
Gallbladder Risk
  • Resmetirom: ↑ cholelithiasis/cholecystitis (0.9% vs 0.3% placebo)
  • Semaglutide: Increased gallbladder events (class effect)
Treatment Discontinuation Rates
  • Resmetirom 100 mg: 6.8% due to adverse events
  • Resmetirom 80 mg: 1.9% due to adverse events
  • Semaglutide: 2.6% due to adverse events
Safety and Baseline Risk Assessment
Required Baseline Evaluations (Table 5)
General Considerations
  • Adherence to lifestyle recommendations
  • Alcohol intake assessment (AUDIT-C, alcohol biomarkers)
  • Functional status evaluation
  • Concomitant medications review
Liver Disease Assessment
  • Use NITs to identify fibrosis stages 2–3
  • Exclude cirrhosis
  • Exclude other liver disease
Cardiometabolic Assessment
  • Type 2 diabetes/glycemic levels
  • Body weight/waist circumference ratios
  • Lipid profile
  • Blood pressure
  • Clinical evidence of heart failure, CV disease, or CKD
Resmetirom-Specific Safety
  • Thyroid function tests
  • Drug-drug interactions (statins, clopidogrel)
  • Gallbladder/biliary disease history
Semaglutide-Specific Safety
  • Thyroid C-cell tumors/MEN2 screening
  • Diabetes-related eye disease (proliferative diabetic retinopathy)
  • History of pancreatitis
  • Anthropometric profile/body composition assessment for sarcopenia risk
  • Kidney function
  • Gallbladder disease history
  • Severe GI disorders (e.g., gastroparesis)
Monitoring Strategy
Resmetirom Follow-Up Schedule
  • Months 3, 6, 12: Adverse events and liver blood tests
  • Beyond Year 1: Every 6 months or per clinical needs
Thyroid Function Monitoring (Resmetirom)
  • Only recommended in adults with history of hyper/hypothyroidism or on thyroid hormone replacement
  • First year: Every 3 months
  • After first year: Annually if stable
Semaglutide Titration Schedule (Table 6)
Weeks Dose
1–4 0.25 mg/week
5–8 0.5 mg/week
9–12 1 mg/week
13–16 1.7 mg/week
After 16 2.4 mg/week (maintenance)
Follow-Up Tests Summary (Table 7)
All Patients
  • Fibrosis NIT: Initial, then every 12 months
  • Liver function panel (AST, ALT, GGT, bilirubin, INR, platelets): Initial, then every 6 months
  • Body weight/BMI: Every 6 months
  • Nutritional intake, physical activity: Initial, then every 3–6 months
  • Side effects: Every 3 months
Semaglutide-Specific Monitoring
  • Glycemic levels: Every 3 months (in T2D patients)
  • Muscle strength/mass: Every 6 months
  • Vitamins: Every 6 months (especially if rapid weight loss)
  • Retinal exam in T2D patients
Resmetirom-Specific Monitoring
  • Lipid profile: Annually
  • Thyroid function: Every 12 months (only if on thyroid hormone replacement)
NIT Response Criteria (Table 8)
  • VCTE-LSM decrease >30%: Correlates with fibrosis improvement
  • MRE-LSM decrease >20%: Lower decompensation in small studies
  • MRI-PDFF decrease >30%: Correlates with MASH resolution and NAS reduction
  • ELF decrease >0.5 units: Lower progression to cirrhosis/decompensation
  • ALT decrease >17 U/L: Correlates with NAS reduction
Semaglutide: Sarcopenia and Nutritional Concerns
  • Rapid weight loss --> risk of skeletal muscle mass/function loss
  • Greater clinical impact in patients with liver disease (already prone to sarcopenia)
  • Protein intake recommendations:
  • Weight loss phase: 1.2–1.5 g/kg/day or 25–30% of daily energy intake
  • Weight maintenance: >0.8 g/kg/day
  • Sarcopenia/sarcopenic obesity/elderly: >1.0–1.2 g/kg/day
  • Calculate protein needs based on adjusted body weight: IBW + 0.25 × (actual − IBW)
  • Recommend resistance/strength training during GLP-1RA therapy
Treatment Discontinuation Criteria (Fig. 3)
Immediate Discontinuation Required
Resmetirom
  • Suspected hepatotoxicity
  • AST/ALT >8× ULN, OR
  • AST/ALT >5× ULN for >2 weeks, OR
  • Total bilirubin >2.5 mg/dl with elevated AST/ALT/ALP, OR
  • INR >1.5 plus elevated liver enzymes
  • Gallbladder-related adverse events (until resolved)
Semaglutide
  • Acute pancreatitis
  • Acute kidney injury (mainly due to dehydration)
  • Intestinal obstruction
  • Severe gastroparesis
  • Gallbladder disease
  • Thyroid C-cell tumor
Treatment Response Assessment
Resmetirom
  • Assess after 12 months
  • If liver fibrosis NITs improve --> continue treatment
  • If evidence of worsening liver fibrosis after 12 months --> consider discontinuation
Semaglutide
  • Assess after 18 months
  • If evidence of worsening liver fibrosis --> consider alternative MASH treatment
  • Continuation may be considered after comprehensive assessment of cardiometabolic benefits
Stable Disease Management
  • If stable but no fibrosis improvement after 12 months (resmetirom) or 18 months (semaglutide):
  • Treatment may be continued
  • Individualized optimization of cardiometabolic risk factors recommended
Worsening Fibrosis Workup
  • Lifestyle reassessment (alcohol, diet, exercise)
  • Alcohol biomarkers (phosphatidylethanol)
  • Metabolic assessment:
  • Glycemic levels
  • Body weight changes
MASH-Related Compensated Cirrhosis
Current Approval Status
  • Both resmetirom and semaglutide are not approved for cirrhosis (fibrosis stage 4)
  • Limited to those with NIT findings or histology compatible with stage 2–3 fibrosis
Safety in Cirrhosis
  • Semaglutide: No unexpected adverse events; GI side effects similar to non-cirrhotic patients
  • In 120 participants with cirrhosis: discontinuation rate 7.4% vs 3.6% for placebo
  • Resmetirom: In 122 participants with compensated MASH cirrhosis (2-year data):
  • No particular safety concerns
  • Discontinuation rate for adverse events: only 2.5%
Efficacy in Cirrhosis
  • Semaglutide (48-week trial, n=71): No histological benefit over placebo
  • Resmetirom (2-year data):
  • Mean VCTE-LSM decreased by 6.7 kPa
  • 51% experienced >25% reduction in liver stiffness
  • 35% transitioned from F4 to values consistent with stage 3 fibrosis
  • PRO-C3 levels decreased by 40%
  • CSPH risk reduced from 34% to 13% (using Baveno VII criteria)
Recommendations for Cirrhosis
  • Resmetirom or semaglutide should not be used as MASH-targeted treatment until further data available
  • Semaglutide may be used for registered indications (T2D, weight management) in compensated MASH cirrhosis
Combination Therapy
First-Line Recommendation
  • Initiation of combination therapy (resmetirom + semaglutide) as first-line cannot currently be recommended
Adding Resmetirom to Existing GLP-1RA
  • Adults on stable GLP-1RA therapy who meet MASH criteria:
  • Switch to semaglutide 2.4 mg weekly, OR
  • Add resmetirom as MASH-targeted pharmacotherapy
Drug Combinations (Fig. 4)
Compatible Without Restrictions
  • SGLT2 inhibitors: Resmetirom retains efficacy and safety
  • Statins with resmetirom: Requires dose adjustments (caps apply)
  • Other cardiometabolic drugs ( DPP-4i, metformin, glitazones)
Requires Dose Adjustments
  • Clopidogrel + resmetirom: Resmetirom dose reduction required
  • Statins + resmetirom: Caps apply
Risk of Hypoglycemia (Monitor)
  • Sulfonylureas
  • Insulin
Evidence Summary
  • Resmetirom is effective and safe in people on stable GLP-1RA and SGLT2 inhibitors
  • No evidence on semaglutide effectiveness in people already receiving resmetirom
Long-Term Outcomes and Ongoing Trials
Key Ongoing Registrational Trials
MAESTRO-NASH Outcomes (Resmetirom)
  • ~700 participants with compensated cirrhosis
  • Expected results: 2027/2028
  • Purpose: Support expanded indication for resmetirom in cirrhosis
MAESTRO-NASH Phase III (Resmetirom)
  • Stage 2–3 fibrosis participants
  • Tracking for 54 months
  • Purpose: Full regulatory approval
ESSENCE Trial (Semaglutide)
  • ~1,200 participants with stage 2–3 fibrosis
  • 240 weeks total (Part 1: histological endpoints at 72 weeks; Part 2: clinical outcomes)
  • Expected results for long-term assessment: 2029
  • Primary endpoint: Liver-related clinical events (progression to cirrhosis, transplantation, liver-related death)
Real-World Evidence for GLP-1RAs
  • Meta-analysis of 11 cohort studies (n=1,467,220 with T2D):
  • MALO incidence rate ratio: 0.71 (95% CI: 0.57–0.88)
  • Hepatic decompensation rate ratio: 0.70 (95% CI: 0.52–0.94)
  • Lower MALO rates vs SGLT2 inhibitors but not vs DPP-4 inhibitors
Semaglutide and Alcohol Reduction
  • RCT in obesity and alcohol use disorder:
  • 41% reduction in heavy drinking vs 26% with placebo
  • Retrospective analysis of US Veterans health records:
  • Lower risk of liver-related outcomes (HR 0.50, 95% CI: 0.29–0.88)
  • Lower odds of harmful alcohol use (OR 0.75, 95% CI: 0.68–0.82)
Cardiovascular Outcomes
Semaglutide
  • SUSTAIN-6 (T2D, 0.5–1 mg weekly): HR 0.74 (95% CI: 0.58–0.95) for MACE
  • SELECT trial (obesity, 2.4 mg weekly): HR 0.79 (95% CI: 0.63–0.98) for MACE
  • Pre-specified analysis in participants at high liver fibrosis risk (FIB-4): Similar CV benefit
  • STEP trials: 50% of participants discontinued semaglutide in first year (real-world)
Resmetirom
  • No long-term CV outcome data available
  • MAESTRO-NASH phase III not powered for MACE detection
Figures
Fig. 1: General pathway for identifying adults with MASHL eligible for MASH-targeted pharmacotherapy and for informing choice of treatment. MASH-targeted pharmacotherapy is currently only indicated for individuals with MASH and stage 2-3 fibrosis. Fibrosis should be determined primarily by non-invasive tests, but liver biopsy may be used in selected cases. The choice of pharmacotherapy integrates clinical data, primarily the individual cardiometabolic risk and other anticipated morbidity profile, the expected hepatic and non-hepatic benefits vs. risks and side effects associated with the drug and its mode of action, and their anticipated magnitude. ELF, enhanced liver fibrosis; MASH, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis; MRE, magnetic resonance elastography; NIT, non-invasive test; T2D, type 2 diabetes; VCTE, vibration-controlled transient elastography.
Fig. 2: Fig. 2. Decision pathway for choosing MASH-targeted pharmacotherapy for treatment-eligible adults with MASH fibrosis. Adults with MASH and stage 2 or 3 fibrosis on histology or fibrosis NT readings compatible with significant or advanced fibrosis have a principal indication for MASH-targeted pharmacotherapy. Clinical scenarios are given which may help to guide the choice of a specific treatment option, based on an individualized decision process tailored to the individual treatment candidate. CKD, chronic kidney disease; ELF, enhanced liver fibrosis; GLP-1RA, glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist; MASH, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis; MRE, magnetic resonance elastography; NET, non-invasive test; T2D, type 2 diabetes; VCTE, vibration-controlled transient elastography.

Adults with MASH and stage 2 or 3 fibrosis on histology or fibrosis NT readings compatible with significant or advanced fibrosis have a principal indication for MASH-targeted pharmacotherapy. Clinical scenarios are given which may help to guide the choice of a specific treatment option, based on an individualized decision process tailored to the individual treatment candidate. CKD, chronic kidney disease; ELF, enhanced liver fibrosis; GLP-1RA, glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist; MASH, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis; MRE, magnetic resonance elastography; NET, non-invasive test; T2D, type 2 diabetes; VCTE, vibration-controlled transient elastography.
Table 7: Follow-up tests for adults treated with resmetirom or semaglutide.
Fig. 3: Decision pathway for continuation or discontinuation of MASH-targeted pharmacotherapy. Adults on MASH-targeted pharmacotherapy should be monitored for hepatotoxicity, major adverse liver outcomes, intolerability and severe treatment-related adverse events. If any of these occur, treatment should be stopped. Treatment effects should be assessed after 12 months and once every year thereafter using NITs for fibrosis. While treatment should be continued if liver fibrosis NITs improve, the decision whether to continue or discontinue treatment in those with stable or worsening NITs should take into consideration cardio-renal-metabolic benefits for those on semaglutide. If treatment needs to be stopped, or if treatment is continued despite stable or worsening liver fibrosis NITs, alternative treatment options for MASH need to be considered and treatment for cardiometabolic risk factors should be optimised. MASH, metabolic dysfunction-associated steat hepatitis; MALO, major adverse liver outcome; NIT, non-invasive test.
Fig. 4: Commonly-prescribed medications for the treatment of cardiometabolic comorbidities and risk factors, and their combination with the approved MASH-targeted drugs resmetrom and semaglutide. Green tick: combination is possible without formal restrictions, yellow tick: potential interactions that require dose adjustments; red cross: should not be combined. DPP4, dipeptidyl peptidase 4 inhibitor(s); GLP-1RA, glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist(s); MASH, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis; SGLT2i, sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor(s).
